How I can help

Support that meets you where you are

Every person who comes to therapy is different. Here are some of the areas I work with most often — each session is shaped around you, not a script.

Young people (10+)

A gentle, age-appropriate space for teenagers navigating anxiety, self-esteem, school pressure, friendships or big feelings — with parents kept sensitively in the loop.

Nature-informed therapy

Where helpful, we bring the natural world into our work — grounding exercises, outdoor sessions by arrangement, and the steadying rhythm of the seasons.

Creative & art-based work

For those who find words difficult, we can draw on gentle creative and expressive techniques alongside talking — no artistic skill required, ever.

Anxiety, stress & life transitions

Support for adults through change, overwhelm, low mood, grief or burnout — practical, compassionate, and paced around you.

My approach

Rooted like a tree, open like the sky

I believe good therapy feels less like being fixed, and more like being tended — with patience, honesty and room to grow at your own pace. My approach blends established psychotherapeutic practice with three quiet influences: nature, for perspective and grounding; art, for expression beyond words; and peace, as something we build together, session by session.

Whether you're a teenager finding your footing, a parent worried about your child, or an adult facing a difficult season, you'll find a space here that is unhurried, non-judgemental and entirely your own.

Therapy gave my daughter somewhere to put everything she couldn't say out loud. She looked forward to every session — that alone told us we'd found the right person. — Parent of a young client. Shared with permission; identifying details changed to protect confidentiality.

My story

Why I became a therapist

[This is where your own story goes — replace freely.] From an early age I was drawn to the outdoors and to making things, and I noticed how often a walk in the woods or an hour spent painting said more than words ever could. That noticing became a career: I trained as an integrative psychotherapist because I wanted to offer people — especially young people — a space that didn't ask them to perform wellness, only to be honest.

I've worked with teenagers and adults across school, community and private practice settings, supporting people through anxiety, low self-esteem, family change, grief and the ordinary, exhausting business of growing up. I still believe the best therapy borrows a little from nature's patience: nothing is rushed, and everything is allowed its season.

Outside sessions, you'll usually find me walking, sketching, or pottering in the garden — the same quiet pursuits I gently bring into the therapy room when it's helpful.

A note on safe practice

I work within the BACP's Ethical Framework for the Counselling Professions, and I'm committed to ongoing continuing professional development (CPD) each year. I attend regular clinical supervision with an experienced supervisor to make sure my practice stays safe, reflective and accountable — this is a requirement of my professional body, not an optional extra.

When working with clients under 18, I follow clear safeguarding procedures and UK child protection guidance, and I'm always happy to talk parents/carers through how confidentiality works before we begin.

What guides me

My values in practice

Nature

Growth isn't linear, and neither is healing. I take my cue from the natural world: steady, seasonal, and never in a hurry.

Art

Not every feeling has a sentence. Creative expression gives us another language when talking alone isn't enough.

Peace

My aim isn't to hurry you towards answers, but to help you build a calmer, steadier relationship with yourself.

Common questions

Fees & practicalities, answered

How many sessions will I need?

It varies enormously from person to person. Some clients find six to eight sessions enough to work through a specific issue; others prefer ongoing, open-ended support. We'll review progress together regularly, and there's never any obligation to continue.

Do you offer online sessions?

Yes — most sessions take place over a secure video platform, which many clients (especially teenagers) find comfortable and convenient. In-person sessions can be arranged by request.

What if my teenager doesn't want to talk?

Completely normal, and nothing to worry about. Sessions with young people are paced gently, and creative approaches often help when talking feels difficult at first.

Is what we discuss confidential?

Yes, with a small number of legal and safety exceptions that I'll always explain clearly at the start of our work together — this is covered in more detail on a free call.
